sections.h2: How can I sell a house fast in Longview, Texas?
sections.html:
Longview sellers choose among an agent listing, a private sale and a cash buyer who takes the house as it is. A listing usually reaches the most buyers, while a cash sale is the quickest way to close when repairs, liens, tenants or an inherited estate stand in the way.

Longview is the seat of Gregg County, on Interstate 20 and U.S. highways 80 and 259, about 125 miles east of Dallas. The city spreads across the Gregg and Harrison county line, which matters for a seller: taxes, deeds and records depend on which county the parcel sits in.

  • Confirm the county first, since a Gregg County house and a Harrison County house use different appraisal and clerk offices.
  • Gather the deed, any mortgage payoff statement and the latest tax bill before you ask for offers.
  • Weigh any cash offer against what a listing would net after repairs, commission and months of carrying costs.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Longview's housing stock?
sections.html:
Longview began in the early 1870s as a railroad town, and its houses show several distinct building eras. The Texas State Historical Association says the Southern Pacific, later the Texas and Pacific, laid out the town about a mile west of the older community of Earpville, and the city incorporated on May 17, 1871.

The East Texas oilfield discovery of the early 1930s spared Longview the worst of the Great Depression. The same account says the population more than doubled that decade, reaching 13,758 in 1940. Postwar growth followed: 24,502 residents in 1950, 40,050 in 1960 and 62,762 in 1980, helped by annexing neighboring Greggton and Spring Hill.

Much of the post-1940 housing comes from that boom, so many Longview homes now carry the age-related repairs a buyer inspects closely: roofs, foundations, old wiring and plumbing.

sections.h2: What drives Longview's economy and its home buyers?
sections.html:
Longview's economy grew from cotton, lumber and the railroad into oil, chemicals, manufacturing and health care. The Handbook of Texas lists the Big Inch pipeline, which began from Longview in 1942 and carried crude oil to the East Coast through 1945, along with a large earth-moving equipment plant and a chemical complex that became the largest in inland Texas.

The same entry calls Longview an important regional industrial and medical center, and notes it is served by the Longview, Pine Tree and Spring Hill independent school districts, each with a major high school. School district matters because it sets part of the tax bill and often a buyer's first search filter.

For a seller, an industrial and medical economy means a steady stream of relocating workers, but also a market that follows oil and manufacturing cycles. A house in a good school district may sell more quickly, while one with deferred maintenance might move faster to a cash buyer.

sections.h2: Who values the property and sends the tax bill in Longview?
sections.html:
The Gregg County Appraisal District values property in Gregg County, and it describes its job as appraising all real and business personal property in the county under the Texas Property Tax Code. Parcels on the Harrison County side are handled by that county's own appraisal district, so confirm which office covers your address.

Gregg's district reported that it would run a reappraisal of residential property from July 2026 to March 2027, with on-site inspections and updated photographs. Appraisers carry a pictured ID, a business card and a state licensing registration card, and a door hanger is left if nobody is home.

For an exemption, the district lists three basic conditions: you own and live in the home on the request date, no residence homestead is claimed elsewhere by you or your spouse, and you give a copy of a Texas driver's license or state ID showing the same address. The district's taxpayer liaison office is at 4367 W Loop 281 in Longview, and its listed phone is 903-238-8823.

sections.h2: What property tax dates and relief programs apply to a Longview seller?
sections.html:
Longview owners follow the statewide calendar. Value and the tax lien are fixed on January 1, a protest deadline lands in mid-May, and bills go out about October 1. Late-January is the last safe payment date, and from February 1 a collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

  • School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value, with a further $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.
  • Disabled veterans receive tiered partial exemptions, and a 100 percent rating can mean a total exemption on the homestead.
  • Heirs missing from a recorded deed can submit an ownership affidavit to the district to claim the exemption.

At a sale, the title company divides the year's bill between buyer and seller. An open lien gets a payoff request and is cleared from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What if I owe back taxes or face foreclosure in Longview?
sections.html:
Call the lender or tax office before a deadline, since both processes move on fixed steps. A Texas deed of trust lets a lender sell without a court, but only after a default notice with a twenty-day cure period and a sale notice three weeks ahead of an auction held early in a month.

Afterward, a lender may sue for a shortfall within two years. Redemption is narrow: for tax sales, a Texas Supreme Court opinion on the court system's site describes two years for homestead, farm or mineral property and 180 days for other land.

Closing a sale before the auction often leaves an owner better off than the auction price would. Ask the title company for payoff amounts and lien balances in writing.

sections.h2: How do I handle an inherited or rented house in Longview?
sections.html:
Begin with the deed. If the owner has died, work out whether probate is needed: a will can be probated for four years after death, and a muniment of title can pass real estate where the estate owes nothing beyond real-estate liens.

For a rented house, expect three days' written notice, a justice court filing, service on the tenant four days ahead of trial and a writ of possession six days after judgment. That schedule is why many owners sell with the tenant in place.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded for a Longview sale?
sections.html:
File the deed in the county where the land lies, Gregg or Harrison for a Longview address. The clerk records it only after the signature is acknowledged by a notary or similar officer.

Clerk fees run $5.00 on page one and $4.00 per added page under the state manual, with separate records charges. Closing funds normally cover them, and your job is to check that the legal description matches the deed of record.

faqs.q: Which county handles a Longview house, Gregg or Harrison?
faqs.a: It depends on where the parcel sits, because Longview lies in both counties. Check your tax bill or deed: the appraisal district named there is the office to deal with, and the deed is recorded with that county's clerk.

faqs.q: Can a lien stop a Longview sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company requests payoff amounts and pays liens from your sale proceeds at closing. A buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent property taxes are paid.

faqs.q: When do Longview property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Most Texas property taxes turn delinquent on February 1 if unpaid. A six percent penalty and one percent interest are added then, and the penalty grows monthly through July 1.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Longview house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. Cash buyers purchase as-is, though the price reflects the repairs the buyer expects to make. Get an offer and compare it with a repaired-and-listed price before choosing.

faqs.q: How long does Texas foreclosure take once I get a notice?
faqs.a: The notice of default gives 20 days to cure, and a notice of sale must come at least 21 days before the auction. Sales are held on the first Tuesday of a month, so the timeline can be short.
